chapter: Leaving home: Fisk, Tulsa, Arkansas City
title: Playing duo with guitar and the Burton Brothers' club
summary: Playing with just a guitar taught him a lot about filling in; he names the Cedars Club, also called the Burton Brothers Club, run by Clyde and Babe Burton.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, Jay, if you had to fill in with the guitar, you had to do a lot more filling in that you would have to do with a band.
Uh-huh. Well, that's really what happened. It helped me a lot because with just the two of us there, we had, you know, we had --
I mean, you don't get much melody off the guitar.
That's right. And so I -- that's when after they closed the club there in that particular town --
What was the name of that club?
What would they call it? That was -- let me see, that was the Cedars Club that Lee Deere had. And they just called it the Burton Brothers Club when I was there, you know, Burton Brothers Club.
When you mentioned Clyde Burton, who was he?
Didn't you say -- who did you say --
Clyde Burton and Babe Burton. Those were the two fellas I worked for, the two brothers.
Oh, I see. Were they well known for anything besides running this place?
Well, I imagine they run a lot of booze in their days and things like that.
Well, you spoke of them as though they were kind of important.
Well, to the going people, people that go to clubs and things like that, they were well known. They were, you know, like club people, they says, "Well, I'm going out to Babe's," you know.

And then you really get a chance to see how well known they were, you know, as well as Lee Deere being so well known. So they had consequently, they had the town wrapped up and there never were anybody else come in there and making the competition.
